story: Every leaf owns a rectangle of the feature plane. Move a probe across the borders: the root cut spans the plane, but the next cut belongs only to the right-hand region.

aha.observation: The horizontal y cut divides only x > 4. J falls in the lower-right class-0 leaf, alongside training row E.

controls.label: Probe x
controls.effect: Move the probe horizontally and change its leaf when it crosses x = 4.

controls.label: Probe y
controls.effect: Move the probe vertically; the y cut changes predictions only on the right.

controls.label: Build the partition
controls.effect: Show no cut, the root cut, or both fitted cuts and recompute the reached region.
Restore the declared initial inputs and the initial evidence.

data.title: The next cut stays in its branch.
data.heading: Probe the fitted decision regions
data.prompt: how does a decision tree split a two-feature dataset into regions?
data.instructions: Try (6, 1), then move left across x = 4. Compare where the horizontal cut applies.
calculations: Root region uses the source test x≤4; the right-child test is y≤2.
Before any cut, predict majority 0. After the root cut, the right child predicts majority 1.
Region membership and class counts are recomputed from source rows; equality follows the ≤ branch.
